summary: This work measures quasiparticle-induced transition rates in fluxonium qubits under controlled on-chip injection and demonstrates that superconducting gap asymmetry $\delta\Delta/h \approx 1.72$ GHz across Josephson junction leads is essential for explaining the external flux dependence of these rates. The results show that accounting for $\delta\Delta$ resolves previously reported discrepancies between quasiparticle density bounds in the small junction versus the junction array, yielding consistent $x_{\mathrm{qp}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ across both elements.
motivation: Quasiparticles are a major decoherence source in superconducting qubits, but their effects are difficult to isolate in fluxonium due to charge insensitivity that precludes charge-parity detection. Prior studies have reported puzzling discrepancies: bounds on $x_{\mathrm{qp}}^{\mathrm{small}}$ typically exceed $x_{\mathrm{qp}}^{\mathrm{array}}$ by orders of magnitude, but the origin of this disparity remained unclear.
method: The authors performed controlled QP injection via a voltage-biased junction and measured quasi-instantaneous excitation and de-excitation rates $\Gamma_{\uparrow,\downarrow}$ at flux bias points ranging from integer flux quantum (IFQ, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$) to half-integer flux quantum (HFQ, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=0.5\Phi_0$). Background-subtracted QP-induced rates $\Delta\Gamma_{\downarrow,\uparrow} = \Gamma^{\mathrm{inj}} - \Gamma^{\mathrm{bg}}$ were modeled with $\delta E_{\mathrm{qp}} \sim \hbar\omega_{01} \sim k_B T_{\mathrm{qp}}/h \approx 1.2$ GHz and $\delta\Delta \neq 0$, independently measured from the resonant peak in $\Gamma_{02}$ at $\hbar\omega_{02} \approx \delta\Delta$.
result: For qubit Q1 ($E_J/h=2.043$ GHz, $E_L/h=0.078$ GHz), one-parameter fits to $\Delta\Gamma_{\downarrow}$ assuming equal QP densities $x_{\mathrm{qp}}^{\mathrm{small}}=x_{\mathrm{qp}}^{\mathrm{array}}$ yielded $x_{\mathrm{qp}}=3.6 \times 10^{-6}$, consistent with the independent transmon measurement $x_{\mathrm{qp}}^{\mathrm{tr}}=3.0 \times 10^{-6}$. The two-peak structure in $\Delta\Gamma_{\downarrow}(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}})$ with comparable magnitudes at IFQ and HFQ—inconsistent with prior models assuming $\delta\Delta=0$—is explained by suppression near HFQ via the condition $\delta E_{\mathrm{qp}} \lesssim \delta\Delta - \hbar\omega_{01}$.
